newsitem.title: GREECE: GREEK SHARES CLIMB AS VOLUME PICKS UP.
newsitem.headline: GREEK SHARES CLIMB AS VOLUME PICKS UP.

text.p: Greek stocks came off their highs on Wednesday but still settled with gains of 0.65 percent on improved trading volume which was boosted by block trades. Construction led the advance with gains of 2.12 percent.

"The market proves that despite the summer doldrums there is considerable underlying interest in blue chip banks, metallurgical and industrials, also lifting OTE telecom from recent oversold levels," said Nick Kontorozis, analyst at Euroxx Securities.
"This keeps downside risk very low and the index corrects at a mild pace," he added.
Salomon Brothers downgraded Greek stocks to underweight short term and neutral long term in its August emerging Europe strategy report from neutral short and long term a month earlier.
It said Greek equities had become expensive with a market price earnings ratio (P/E) of 12 and expected further correction for the rest of the year.
"Greek shares remain attractive based their on P/E multiple and prospects for accelerating profit growth," Euroxx's Kontorozis said.
The banking sector is even more appealing with a far lower price to earnings valuation and above average earnings growth, he added.
The Athens benchmark index advanced 0.65 percent or 10.68 points to 1,642.36 from Tuesday's 1,631.68, easing from an intra-day high at 1,648.98.
Construction led the market with a 2.12 percent rise, followed by banks which were up 0.98 percent.

Turnover grew to 9.3 billion drachmas on volume of 2.4 million shares. Blocks were traded in Alpha Credit Bank, 35,000 shares at 20,110 drachmas, National Bank, 10,000 shares at 37,705, and Ergobank, 13,915 shares at 17,800.
Advancers beat decliners 124 to 77 with 30 shares unchanged on 231 traded.
OTE telecom Global Depository Shares (GDS) were quoted on London's SEAQ International market at $11.0-$11.2. Two GDSs make up one share of OTE.
The Merrill Lynch call spread warrant on OTE with a strike price of 3,800 drachmas, capped at 5,000 drachmas, was quoted at 1,129-1,159 drachmas.

The recently launched second Merrill Lynch call spread warrant on OTE with a strike price of 6,800 drachmas, capped at 10,000 drachmas, was quoted at 1,127-1,187 drachmas. The warrants expire December 16, 1998. Shares of the underlying stock firmed 75 drachmas to 6,575.
The Merrill Lynch American call warrant on a basket of 23 Greek equities that are part of the Athens general index was quoted at 688.56-732.52 drachmas. The warrants expire January 9 1998.

The ING Baring Financial Products American style call warrant based on a basket of six bank stocks was quoted at $76.66-$79.50. The strike price is set at $99.60 and the warrants expire October 8, 1997.

The ING Baring Financial Products American-style call warrant on a basket of six blue-chips denominated in drachmas was quoted at 3,919-4,150 drachmas. The strike price is set at 10,000 drachmas and the warrants expire on February 2, 1998.
The ING Baring American-style second call warrant on a basket of six bank stocks was quoted at $12.54 bid/no offer. The strike price is set at $110.0 and the warrants expire April 9 1998.

The recently launched ING Baring American-style, drachma- denominated call warrant on the bourse's benchmark index was quoted at 247-280 drachmas. The strike price is set at 1,639 points and the warrants expire May 14 1998. --Angelos Kiosklis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
